$comment: The fixed gap-detection taxonomy (D3): every discovery run walks exactly these questions per unit kind, so two runs over the same sources raise the same questions. Q-ids are a citation namespace — scripts/citations.mjs (repo root) resolves every Q-id cited in prose against this register. defaultHint is the seed of the conservative default (D4), specialized to the unit's evidence at generation time.

questions.question: When the data behind this screen fails to load, or an action on it fails, what does the user see and what can they do next?
questions.defaultHint: Show an inline error state with a retry action; never a blank screen or a silent failure.

questions.question: What does this screen show when there is no data yet, and how does the user get from that state to the first record?
questions.defaultHint: Show a dedicated empty state that names the primary action; never an empty table frame.

questions.question: What does this screen show while its data is loading, and which parts stay interactive?
questions.defaultHint: Show a loading state in place of the pending region; keep navigation interactive; never block the whole page.

questions.question: Which roles may see this screen, and which of its actions are restricted to which roles?
questions.defaultHint: The screen is visible to every role the brief names; write and destructive actions require the most privileged named role until stated otherwise.

questions.question: For each input on this screen, what are the validation rules, and where and when are violations shown?
questions.defaultHint: Required fields must be non-empty; formats are validated at the boundary; violations show inline per field on submit.

questions.question: Which actions on this screen are destructive or irreversible, and which of them require explicit confirmation?
questions.defaultHint: Any delete or irreversible action asks for explicit confirmation in a dialog; non-destructive actions act immediately with an undo affordance.

questions.question: Where does this screen's copy come from, and which locales must it exist in?
questions.defaultHint: All copy comes from the i18n catalogue; English is the only locale until the brief names another.

questions.question: How do long values, long lists and narrow viewports behave on this screen?
questions.defaultHint: Long text truncates with the full value reachable; long lists paginate or scroll within the region; the layout wraps at narrow widths instead of overflowing.

questions.question: Who initiates this flow, and what exactly triggers it?
questions.defaultHint: The least privileged role the brief names initiates it through an explicit user action; nothing starts it implicitly.

questions.question: What observable outcome means this flow succeeded, and what does the user see at that moment?
questions.defaultHint: The flow ends on a visible confirmation of the created or changed record; success is observable, never assumed.

questions.question: What happens when this flow fails midway, and what happens when the user abandons it?
questions.defaultHint: A midway failure preserves the user's input and states what failed; abandoning discards nothing without confirmation.

questions.question: What side effects does this flow have beyond its primary record — notifications, derived data, external calls?
questions.defaultHint: No side effects beyond the primary record until one is stated; every stated side effect is listed in the flow's document.

questions.question: Which operations does this area expose, and what are their request and response shapes?
questions.defaultHint: One CRUD set per entity with shapes derived from the entity's fields; no operation beyond what the sources state.

questions.question: Which system is the source of truth for this area's data, and who may write it?
questions.defaultHint: This service owns its data; external systems read through the contract and never write directly.

questions.question: How do callers authenticate, and which caller may invoke which operation?
questions.defaultHint: Every operation requires authentication; write operations additionally require the owning role; nothing is anonymous until stated.

questions.question: What error shapes can this area return, and are they stable enough for a consumer to program against?
questions.defaultHint: Every error is a registered RFC 9457 problem type with a stable type URI — the BR-23 catalogue discipline.

questions.question: How do list operations paginate, sort and filter, and what are the limits?
questions.defaultHint: List operations paginate with an explicit page size and a documented maximum; sorting and filtering exist only where stated.

questions.question: Which operations are idempotent, and what happens when a client retries a write?
questions.defaultHint: Reads and deletes are idempotent; creates accept an idempotency key so a retry cannot double-write.

questions.question: How long is this area's data kept, which fields are personal data, and how are they deleted or redacted?
questions.defaultHint: Data is kept until explicitly deleted; fields naming a person are treated as PII, redacted from logs (NFR-12) and deletable on request.

questions.question: For each external system this area touches, what is the agreed contract, and where is it recorded?
questions.defaultHint: Every external system sits behind an adapter with its contract recorded locally with provenance — the BR-18 record discipline.

questions.question: What does the customer actually gain when this ships — the Need-payoff in one falsifiable sentence?
questions.defaultHint: State the gain as an observable change for a named actor; a gain nobody could observe is not a gain.

questions.question: Where does this deploy first, which environments exist in the promotion chain, and who approves promotion?
questions.defaultHint: A dev environment only until the operator enables more; every later environment is a reviewed config change, never a regeneration.

questions.question: Which languages must the product ship in, and which locale is the default?
questions.defaultHint: English only, as the default locale, until the brief names another — a named locale is a commitment to translate (BR-09).

questions.question: Must anything work offline, and must anything update in real time?
questions.defaultHint: Neither, until stated: online-only with explicit refresh is the conservative default for both.
